description: Seaborgium is a synthetic chemical element with symbol Sg and atomic number 106, named after American nuclear chemist Glenn T. Seaborg. It is a d-block transactinide element belonging to group 6 as the fourth member of the 6d series of transition metals in the 7th period. As a synthetic element, it is created in laboratories but not found in nature and is radioactive with the most stable known isotopes having half-lives on the order of several minutes.
uses: Very few chemical reactions of seaborgium have been studied due to the difficulty of producing and isolating the element. A few inorganic compounds and a carbonyl believed to be Sg(CO)6 have been synthesized to investigate seaborgium's chemical properties.
characteristics: Seaborgium is radioactive with no stable or naturally occurring isotopes. Experiments have confirmed that seaborgium behaves as the heavier homologue to tungsten in group 6, and fourteen different radioactive isotopes with mass numbers 257–269 and 271 have been synthesized, all of which decay through alpha decay and spontaneous fission except seaborgium-261 which can also undergo electron capture.
